Lockout Gate uses Accessibility to detect which app is open and show a blocking screen for the apps you select. It does not read screen text, messages or passwords. App selections and usage stay on your phone; nothing is sent to a server.\n\nYou can turn off the service or uninstall the app at any time. Usage Access separately measures time spent in selected apps.

Lockout Gate — Privacy & Help
Updated 19 October 2026

This preview works entirely on your phone. No account, ads, analytics SDK, AI service, payments or server connection is used.

Accessibility detects foreground app package names to show your chosen block screen. It does not retrieve screen text, messages or passwords. Usage Access reads app activity events to count break time. Selected apps, habits and their history stay in private app storage. An optional background image is copied into private app storage. Notifications show remaining break time.

You may refuse permissions, pause protection, change selected apps, disable the service in Android Settings or uninstall at any time. Without Accessibility, app blocking cannot operate. Without Usage Access, breaks cannot be measured reliably. Some phone manufacturers may stop background services.

To remove all local data, clear app storage or uninstall. This cannot be undone. There is no cloud backup. This is a self-control aid, not parental control, a security lock or an emergency restriction. Always keep emergency calls and important system apps available.

A future paid or advertising version will require a separate update and revised disclosures. No payment will begin automatically.
